title: Relative equidimensionality from a flat-associated point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent]. For $s\in S$ let $X_s$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre], $i_s:X_s\to X$ its projection and $\mathcal F_s=i_s^*\mathcal F$. A point $x\in X_s$ is an associated point of $\mathcal F_s$ if the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ is an associated prime [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes] of the stalk $(\mathcal F_s)_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] as an $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$-module. The relative assassin $\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$ is the set of points $x\in X$ which, regarded as points of $X_{f(x)}$, are associated points of $\mathcal F_{f(x)}$. $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$ at $x\in X$ if the stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is a flat $\mathcal O_{S,f(x)}$-module [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Let $y\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$. Let $Y=\overline{\{y\}}\subseteq X$ with its reduced closed-subscheme structure, which is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], and let $T=\overline{\{f(y)\}}\subseteq S$ likewise; $f$ restricts to a dominant morphism $Y\to T$. Assume that $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$ at every generic point [def-sc-generic-point] of every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of every fibre $Y_s$ ($s\in T$) of $Y\to T$. Then (i) every generic point of an irreducible component of a fibre $Y_s$ lies in $\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$, and (ii) there is an integer $d\ge0$ such that $Y\to T$ has relative dimension $d$: every irreducible component of every nonempty fibre $Y_s$ has Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] equal to $d$.

proof.text: Put $t=f(y)$ and write $g:Y\to S$ for the composite of the given closed immersion $Y\hookrightarrow X$ with $f$. An immersion is locally of finite type, composition preserves this property, and base change then makes every fibre $Y_s$ of $g$ locally of finite type over $\kappa(s)$. For $s\in T$, its residue field as a point of $T$ is the same as its residue field in $S$: a quotient local ring has the same residue field. Consequently the fibre of $Y\to T$ is this same $Y_s$, by the defining fibre-product universal property (a map into $T$ is determined by its composite with the closed immersion into $S$). The fibre topology identifies $Y_t$ with $Y\cap f^{-1}(t)$. Its point $y$ is generic: every nonempty relatively open subset contains $y$, since it is the intersection with an open of $X$ meeting $\overline{\{y\}}$. Thus $Y_t$ is nonempty and irreducible.

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine member $U$ of the locally finite type affine cover of $Y_t$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$. Its coordinate algebra is finitely generated over $\kappa(t)$, so $U$ is of finite type over that field by the finite-type definition. Its dimension is finite by the finite-type dimension bound. Apply the irreducible locally algebraic dimension theorem to $Y_t$ and its nonempty open $U$ to get $\dim(Y_t)=\dim U<\infty$. Since $Y_t$ is nonempty, its dimension is not $-\infty$; the chain definition therefore supplies a nonnegative integer $d=\dim(Y_t)$. This argument does not assume that $Y_t$ itself is quasi-compact.

proof.text: Fix any $s\in T$ and any irreducible component $C$ of the fibre $Y_s$. Scheme sobriety supplies its generic point $x$. The hypothesis of the item gives flatness of $\mathcal F$ over the original base $S$ at this $x$. Apply the pointwise specialization theorem to the original morphism $f:X\to S$, its finite type quasi-coherent module $\mathcal F$, the given relative associated point $y$, and this $s,C,x$. All its assumptions are exactly the hypotheses of the item and this pointwise flatness. It gives $x\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$ and $\dim C=\dim(Y_t)=d$. The first assertion is (i); the second holds for every component of every nonempty fibre of $Y\to T$ by step 1, and is precisely (ii) with the equidimensional-fibre convention stated in the item. Empty fibres have no components and impose no condition. The same $d$ is used for all $s$, because it was fixed from $Y_t$ before choosing $s$.

The item's statement is unchanged and matches Stacks 0GSJ (more-morphisms, lemma-flat-associated-equidimensional) hypothesis by hypothesis. Clause (ii) writes out the meaning of Morphisms 02NJ(3), relative dimension d: all nonempty fibres equidimensional of dimension d. Nothing is weakened, and no base-change morphism or coefficient category is involved. Step 1 is correct. It gets locally finite type fibres from three Mathlib-leaf nodes: lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft part (2), lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence part (e) and lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change. The fibre of Y over T is the same as its fibre over S because T->S is a closed immersion with the same residue fields. Y_t is irreducible with y as its generic point. Step 2 is correct. It takes a finite type affine open U and gets dim U finite from lem-kun-dimension-finite-type (Lean-closed). Then dim Y_t = dim U by lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic, which matches Varieties 0A21(3). Y_t is nonempty, so d >= 0, and Y_t is never assumed quasi-compact. Step 3 is correct. lem-sc-scheme-sober gives the generic point x of each component C, and the new pointwise node applies at x. d is fixed before s and C are chosen, and empty fibres impose nothing. The new node lem-trf-flat-relative-associated-specialization is exactly Stacks 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes), which I read in full. Its extra equality dim C = dim Y_t is written in the second paragraph of the 0GSI proof. It is also true on its own terms: the generic point of C lies on no other component of the locally Noetherian fibre Y_s, so dim_x(Y_s) = dim C. The node is statement-only and self-contained, cites a defining node for every notion and records three kinds of search. It is not a relabelling or restatement of the item (D1, D2): it needs flatness only at the one chosen point, it is a separate Stacks lemma that Stacks also uses elsewhere, and the item still has to produce the finite d >= 0 and make it uniform. No blueprint node mentions 0GSI. There is no cycle. The transitive route of unit sk-i-curve-zero contains the Kunneth and Jacobian units. I accept the declared tool uses: lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft, lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence, lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change, lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic and lem-sc-scheme-sober. lean.statement: theorem flat_associated_equidimensional {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (y : X) (hy : y ∈ relativeAssassin f F) (hflat : ∀ (s : closureSubscheme (f y)), ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents ((closureMap f y).fiber s), ∀ x : (closureMap f y).fiber s, IsGenericPoint x C → moduleFlatAt f F (closureInclusion y ((closureMap f y).fiberι s x))) : (∀ (s : closureSubscheme (f y)), ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents ((closureMap f y).fiber s), ∀ x : (closureMap f y).fiber s, IsGenericPoint x C → closureInclusion y ((closureMap f y).fiberι s x) ∈ relativeAssassin f F) ∧ (∃ d : ℕ, ∀ (s : closureSubscheme (f y)), ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents ((closureMap f y).fiber s), topologicalKrullDim C = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
